predecessors.name: County of Waldeck
predecessors.text: Waldeck proper: the districts of the Twiste (Arolsen), the Eisenberg (Korbach) and the Eder (Wildungen)

successors.name: German Empire
successors.text: Waldeck and Pyrmont: the three Waldeck districts and the Pyrmont district; 1,121 km2 in 1905

ledger.x: 1806: the principality continues as a state of the Holy Roman Empire's successors.
1871: the principality becomes a state of the German Empire.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Waldeck 'fought on the Prussian side in the Austro-Prussian War of 1866 and thus avoided annexation'; no territory changed.

certainty.note: A small state with administrative boundaries (three districts from 1849-1850 plus Pyrmont); the pages give no survey, the Pyrmont district lay apart, and the grid cannot draw the Prussian exclaves of Höringhausen and Eimelrod.
